The Committee finds the progress in this regard satisfactory. It urges the Department to continue this pace especially with
respect to the training of technical teachers.     (para 5.3.5)

the future. The Committee also urges the Department to constantly monitor the utilisation of funds by the research institutions to
avoid any such confusion in the future.                                                                               (para 5.3.6)
Comments of the Committee
The Committee further expresses its concern over the development of                nano-technology in India. It has learnt that
there is no proper and structured syllabus as such for nano-technology in India. The Committee, therefore, urges the Department
to evolve a comprehensive programme to develop nano-technology as a future discipline of immense possibilities.     
                                                                                       (para 5.3.7)

The Committee would also like to point out that in its 178
th Report on 'The National Institutes of Technology Bill, 2006',
it had emphasized the need for extending pensionary and other benefits to the staff of the National Institutes of Technology
located at Jalandhar, Kurukshetra and Silchar similar to those being paid to the staff of National Institutes of Technology in the
rest of the country. The Secretary, Department of Higher Education informed during evidence that they were seized of the matter.
The Committee recommends that in view of maintaining parity at the national level in this regard, the staff of these National
Institutes of Technology should also get the same benefits. The Committee further recommends that the decision in this regard
needs to be taken at the earliest.    (para 5.3.8)
Comments of the Committee
The Committee is happy to note that the Department proposes to set up 3 new Indian Institutes of Technology (IITs) in
Bihar, Andhra Pradesh and Rajasthan; 20 new Indian Institutes of Information Technology (IIITs); 2 new Indian Institutes of

Bhopal and Vijayawada. The Committee wishes that the Department completes the procedural formalities in this regard and gives
shape to the proposals in a time bound manner.                                                                             (para 5.3.9)

POLYTECHNICS IN SPECIAL FOCUS DISTRICTS
Comments of the Committee
           The Committee welcomes the initiative of the Department in this regard. The Committee, however, is unable to
comprehend as to how the Department proposes to implement the scheme with a meager allocation of Rs.50 crore during 2007-
08.  The Committee recommends that efforts should be made to open polytechnics in the entire country with special emphasis
on the backward areas.                                  (para 5.4.3)
Comments of the Committee
           The Committee notes that the Task Force on Skill Development was due to submit its Report by the end of February,
2007. The Committee, therefore, desires that the Committee may be apprised of the recommendations as well as the action taken
by the Department in this regard in its Action Taken Report. In the meantime, the Department may forward a copy of the Report
for perusal of the Committee.                          (para 5.4.5)
5.5            SCHEME OF COMMUNITY POLYTECHNICS
Comments of the Committee
The Committee is of the considered opinion that the uneven reach of the Scheme in the Eastern region of the country does
not conform to its objective of securing community/rural development. The Committee, therefore, urges the Department to factor
in this aspect while reviewing the Scheme for the 11
th Plan.                                     (para 5.5.3)

Comments of the Committee
The Committee notes the efforts being made by the Department in the matter. It, however, urges the Department to
expedite the completion of the construction work in respect of the Maharshi Sandipani Rashtriya Ved Vidya Pratisthan, Ujjain. 
The Committee is of the considered opinion that fund constraints come in way of development and research in Sanskrit language.
Sanskrit granths provide vast knowledge that need to be developed further by researches.  The Committee emphasizes the need
for providing more funds for this. The Committee also recommends that emphasis should be given to the development of Sanskrit
from the basic level.                                                      (para 6.3)

            WOMEN IN HIGHER EDUCATION
Comments of the Committee
The Committee does not accept the reply of the Department. While the Department has been prudent enough to realize

therefore, recommends that a proper strategy and programme may be chalked out to benefit the women in higher education.

The Committee welcomes these developments.  The Committee is, however, a bit disappointed to note that only 42 out of
the 100 proposals have been approved by the Department during 2006-07. The Committee urges the Department to speed up the
approval procedure so that all the 104 proposals pending with it could be decided at the earliest. The Committee also recommends
that the Department should strive to ensure that every University in India must have a Women Study Centre or Department. The
Committee further recommends that more allocations be provided for development of Women Study Centres.

PREFACE
 
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Human Resource Development,
having been authorized by the Committee to present the Report on its behalf, do hereby present this Hundred Ninety - fourth
Report of the Committee on the Demands for Grants (Demand No. 103) of the Ministry of Women and Child Development
for the year 2007-08.
 
2.
                  The Committee considered the various documents and relevant papers received from the Ministry of Women and
Child Development and also heard the Secretary and other Officials of that Ministry on the said Demands for Grants in its

REPORT
           
I.            INTRODUCTION
 
1.1       Growth of the economy has to be not only faster but also inclusive to achieve overall human development.   The flow
of benefits should be sufficiently wide spread and equally distributed among all sections of society, especially women and
children.              As per 2001 Census of India, of the total population of 102.9 crores, there are 49.6 crores (48.3%) women.
Women and children (child 0-14 years) constitute 68.6 crores (66.7%).  Development of Women and children is thus of
paramount importance and sets the pace for overall development.
 
1.2       The Ministry of Women and Child Development is the nodal ministry for all matters pertaining to the welfare,
development and empowerment of women and children in the country.  A separate Ministry for Women and Child
Development came into existence from 30
th January 2006 with the enhanced mandate of dealing with not only policy relating
to children and women but also a comprehensive range of programmes relating to child and women development and
protection.
 
1.3            Secretary, in her presentation before the Committee pointed out that plan allocation of Rs. 5793 crore for 2007-08
showed an approximate increase of 20 per cent over allocation of Rs. 4893 crore for 2006-07. This increase was reflected in
five or six major areas, the foremost being the new schemes.  The Integrated Child Protection Scheme (Rs. 95 crores),
Conditional Cash Transfer Scheme for the Girl Child (Rs. 15 crores) Priyadarshini (Rs 10 crores) and Gender Budgeting (Rs.
3 crores). Besides that, additional provision of Rs. 749 crore was proposed for ICDS, for Swayamsiddha Rs. 20 crores, Creche
Scheme and  the Working Women’s Hostel Scheme- additionality of Rs. 10 crore each and lastly Swadhar getting Rs. 7 crore.
Increase in terms of percentage was 19 per cent for Children Schemes and 40 per cent for Women Schemes.

1.4       The Committee was, however, given to understand that this enhanced allocation was much below the projected

the Planning Commission.
 
1.5       The Secretary also informed the Committee that in the overall Budget of Govt. of India for 2007-08, there was an
increase of one per cent in the Gender Budget of the country.  4.8 per cent of the total budget provision for the country was
earmarked for gender budgeting which came to Rs. 31,000 crores. 
 
II.
                BUDGETARY ALLOCATION
 
2.1       Plan allocation for the Ministry has been made at Rs.5793.00 crore in BE 2007-08 against the projected requirement of
Rs.9463.58 crore for Annual Plan 2007-08 which was going to have an adverse impact on sixteen schemes of the Ministry.
 Important among them are ICDS, Gender Budgeting, Integrated Child Protection Scheme (ICPS), Rashtriya Mahila Kosh,
Swadhar, Comprehensive Scheme for Combating Trafficking of Women and Children; and Relief and Rehabilitation of Rape
victims. The Committee would, however, like to point out that under all these schemes, funds have remained more or  less
under-utilised, if the performance during the last three years is taken into account. Underutilization is in those areas where
need is most.  There appear to be great laxity in implementation of these schemes.   The Committee strongly feels that an
assessment of schemes falling behind their targets should be carried out without any further  delay so as to make a justifiable
proposition before the Planning Commission. The Committee understands that this advice has already been given by the
Planning Commission.
 
2.2
              The plan allocation for the year 2006-07 was Rs. 4839.85 crore.  The actual expenditure as reported upto 31 st
December 2006 is Rs. 3140.64 crore which is 58.99% of plan allocation.   The expenditure upto 16 th March, 2007 is Rs.
4286.78 crore which is 88% of plan allocation.   The expenditure on 29 th March, 2007 is 97% of the allocation as reported by
the Secretary during her evidence.
 
2.3       The year 2007-08 marks the beginning of Eleventh Plan period.   The Committee observes that overall performance of
the Ministry during the Tenth Plan can be considered satisfactory, keeping  in view utilization of Rs. 14656.25 crore against
the approved outlay of Rs. 13,780.00 crore. However, separate assessment of women and children-related schemes leads to a
somewhat different position.   Whereas in the case of schemes relating to child development, both physical and financial
targets could be achieved, status of women related schemes having lesser allocation is very discouraging. The Committee
notes that under Central Schemes for women, utilization figures are less than half of the approved outlay.  Against an outlay of
Rs. 971.11 crore, expenditure reported is only Rs. 434.47 crores. Similarly, for central sponsored schemes for women, only
Rs. 130.48 crores could be utilized by the end of Tenth Plan against an allocation of Rs. 275.01 crore.   The Committee is also
constrained to observe that performance   of six schemes of Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment transferred to the
Ministry of Women and Child Development during the Tenth Plan was far from satisfactory. Against an approved   outlay of
Rs. 245.35 crore, only Rs. 166.70 crore could be spent.   The Committee would also like to point out the under the children
sector also, the only exceptions are the Flagship Scheme of ICDS and Creche Scheme.  In case of Training Programme under
ICDS, National Nutrition Mission, allocated funds remained under-utilised/ unutilized.
 
2.4            Committee’s attention has also been drawn by the CAG observations contained in Report No. 1 of 2006, according
to which Test Check of appropriation accounts with reference to re-appropriation orders for 2004-05 revealed that heavy re-
appropriation of funds amounting to Rs. 462 crore were made between the different primary units of re-appropriation
defeating the original purpose/activity as authorized by Parliament.   The Committee apprehends that things may have
remained unchanged in the subsequent years of Tenth Plan also. The Committee thus would like to know the details of
reappropriation of funds made during the last three years and whether the approval of Ministry of Finance was given or not.
The Committee recommends that the emphasis should not be on the quantity of expenditure but on the quality of output that is
coming out of the Schemes/Programmes which is the ultimate objective of all the Schemes/programmes.   The Committee also
emphasizes that re-appropriation is a bad practice of financial management and the Ministry should try to utilize the funds for 
the purposes for which the funds are allocated.
 
2.5       In the light of feedback received about the performance   level during the Tenth Plan period, the Committee would like
to emphasise that every conceivable   measure needs to be taken by the Ministry so that shortfall and deviations from the
prescribed financial norms do not occur during the Eleventh  Plan Period.

The Committee is deeply disturbed by the status of outstanding Utilisation Certificates. As many as 4697 UCs outstanding for
the period 1986-87 to 2001-02 compels the Committee to conclude that role of the Ministry is perhaps confined to only
disbursement of funds. Year after year, Central Funds are being released to State Govts./ implementing agencies.   Ministry’s
efforts for pursuing the matter with the State Governments as well as the State nodal agencies for submission of the pending
UCs on priority basis seem to have made no impact.   The Committee is also not inclined to believe the contention of the
Ministry that  no further grant is released to any NGO/ implementing agency where UCs are pending. This is borne out by the
pertinent  observations made in the  Audit Report No.3 of 2006 (Para No. 1.4) that
“the Certificates of utilization of grants were required to be furnished by the Ministries/Departments concerned
to the Controller General of Accounts in respect of grants released to statutory bodies, non-government
organizations etc. to ensure that grants had been properly utilized for the purpose for which they were
sanctioned. In the case of Ministry of Women and Child Development, 5934 Utilization certificates (UCs)
involving an amount of Rs. 316.04 crore in respect of grants released up to March 2004, which were due by
31st March 2005 are stated to be outstanding at the time of audit.
Audit has observed that the Ministries/Departments before releasing grants to statutory bodies and non-
government organizations did not satisfy themselves about utilization of grants in 85% cases involving 59% of
the total grant released.”
 
2.9       The Committee wonders as to why inspite of guidelines being issued by the Ministry of Finance from time to time and
also Audit observations, pendency of  UCs has been allowed to continue since long.  Pendency for more than two decades
clearly indicates that fiscal management has not been given its due importance so far.  The Committee would once again
emphasize that this issue  should be taken up with the highest authorities at the State level so that old cases are cleared and
also for identification of  the inherent drawbacks/hindrances--systematic, procedural and others.  The Committee may be
furnished details of implementing agencies (state-wise, schemewise) who are yet to submit UCs and the steps taken to
minimise the pending UCs.
 
2.10            Committee has also been observing the availability of unspent balances with the implementing agencies under
different schemes. As a test case, the Committee would like to point out that under the two Centrally Sponsored Schemes,

respectively as on 01.04.06. By 31
st December, 2006, these figures reached to Rs. 156.91 crore and Rs. 15.34 crores under the
two schemes respectively.   State-wise analysis about availability of unspent balances raises doubt about adherence of the
financial norm of releasing of funds only after adjustment of unspent balance from the previous year.
 
2.11     The Committee has been given to understand that to deal with the unspent balance as well as the committed
expenditure, while releasing funds to the grantee institutions (State Governments/UTs/ NGOs), relevant provisions/guidelines
contained in the GFRs and DFPRs as also the instructions dated 8
th August, 2006   issued by the Department of Expenditure, -
which inter-alia stipulate that the unspent balances available with the States and implementing agencies must be taken into
account before further releases are made, are always taken into account.

III.
             INTEGRATED CHILD DEVELOPMENT SERVICES SCHEME (ICDS)
 
3.1
              The ICDS scheme/launched in 1975 aims at holistic development of children below six years and pregnant and
lactating mothers from disadvantaged sections by providing a package of integrated services, comprising of supplementary
nutrition, immunization, health check-up, referral services, pre-school, non-formal education and nutrition and health
education.
 
3.2       Plan allocation under ICDS constituted about 80% of the budget of the Ministry in 2006-07.  Plan allocation of Rs.
4454.52 crore was made in BE 2006-07, reduced to Rs. 4331.48 crore at RE stage.  Against this, expenditure of Rs.3874.86
crore  has been incurred upto 16
th March, 2007. Funds amounting to Rs.123.04 crores from ICDS were reappropriated to the
World Bank assisted ICDS projects.   Against an approved outlay of Rs. 10391.75 crore for ICDS during the Tenth Plan, 
expenditure reported is Rs. 11,883.05 crore.  Trend of allocation indicates that major provision has been made during the last
two years of the Plan Period.  Enhanced Plan allocation of Rs. 5204.00 crores has been made during 2007-08, the first year of
the Eleventh Plan. While appreciating the trend of optimum utilization of allocated funds during the Tenth Plan, the
Committee observes that quantum of unspent balances has also been showing an upward trend.  Unspent balances of Rs. 61.00
crores were available with different States as on 1 st April, 2006 which have increased upto Rs. 156.91 crores by the end of 
December, 2006.
 
3.3       State-wise information made available by the Ministry indicates that following States have the maximum amount of
unspent balances available with them:-

indicating that funds from the previous year were also available with them.   Both the situations indicate that some inherent

time or States simply do not have the capacity to utilize the enhanced allocation.   The Committee understands that there
already exists a comprehensive four-level monitoring mechanism for ICDS.  The Committee can only emphasise that there is a
need for strengthening the monitoring mechanism so as to regulate the flow of funds and judicious utilization thereof.

3.7       On a specific query about the status of AWC buildings in N-E Region, the Committee was informed that while during

3.8       The Committee notes that inspite of no provision for construction of AWC buildings under the Scheme, in view of

conducted by the National Institute of Public Cooperation and Child Development (NIPCCD) (Report published in December,

not known as to any observation about the specific constraints being faced by N-E States in this vital component of ICDS has
been commented upon in the aforesaid study.  If done, the Committee hopes that remedial steps would be initiated   at the
earliest so as to improve the position in N-E Region. The Committee also notes that the following gap areas have been

3.13     The Committee is aware that the ICDS was envisioned as a community participative programme and the components
of the scheme do not provide for the creation of infrastructural facilities.   However, in view of the present dismal status of
AWC buildings and also chronic problem of fund constraints being faced by majority of States, it is now time that providing
infrastructural facilities like construction of pucca building and other related aspects form part of the scheme so that over a
period of time all the AWCs must have pucca building to function.   If the Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan can provide 30% of its
allocation for infrastructure development, the Committee does not find any reason why a particular percentage of the fund
could not be allocated for infrastructure creation under the ICDS. 
 
3.14     The Committee notes that Ministry is doing all out efforts to universalize the ICDS Scheme.  The Secretary submitted
before the Committee that there seems to be a lack of motivation at the grass-root level and there is a case for a much stronger
community participation.              The Committee feels that the Ministry should come forward to revamp, redesign and recast
the ICDS scheme in all possible ways.
 
3.15     It was submitted before the Committee that   delays  happen  in the allocation of funds due to the involvement of RBI,
State Governments and implementing agencies.  When the money is the released by the Central Government first it goes to the
State Government’s account in the RBI.  The State Government in turn takes its own time to send it down, and depending
upon its ways and means position they keep the money for a month or two or three, and then, further pass it down.
 
3.16     The Committee recommends that since the flow of money from the Centre to the Implementing agencies is taking lot
of time, efforts may be made for quicker and expeditious dispersal of money.  If need be, the ICDS scheme may be converted
into a Mission Mode Scheme so that intermediate agencies can be removed.
 
3.17            Supreme Court, vide its order dated 7.10.2004, had inter-alia, directed all the States/UTs that the contractors shall
not be used for supply of nutrition in Anganwadi Centres and funds shall be spent by making use of SHGs and Mahila
Mandals for buying of grains and preparation of meals.  The Committee was informed that 21 States/UTs have so far
furnished information on system of procurement, storage, distribution of supplementary nutrition, involvement of Corporates/
SHGs and duties/responsibilities thereof under ICDS Programme in their States/UTs.  The Committee may like to know
whether any assessment of the impact of the changeover is being studied. The Committee also recommends that the remaining
states should be directed to furnish their feedback at the earliest.
 
3.18     From 2005-2006, the Government of India were to support states upto 50% of the financial norms or 50 % of the
expenditure incurred by thereon for supplementary nutrition whichever is less. Financial norms for supplementary nutrition
fixed in 1991 have been revised in October, 2004, for children from 6 months to 6 years, Rs. 2.00 per day per child and for
severely malnourished children, Rs. 2.70 per child per day.  On  a specific query about the number of children covered under
ICDS and getting nutrition, the Committee was informed that as per Census 2001, total number of children in the age group 0-
6 years is 15.78 crores. Of these, 10.49 crore children have been reported as child population as per Anganwadi Survey
Register under ICDS as on 30.09.06.  The Committee is, however, surprised to note that only 5.43 crore children out of 10.49
crore children under ICDS were getting supplementary nutrition as on 30.09.06.  Such a huge gap between targeted children
and those covered under ICDS and between children under ICDS and getting supplementary nutrition depicts a very dismal
scenario.  If the State-wise figures are analysed, shortfall and gaps are noticed across the country. The Committee is
extremely  disturbed to note that there are States where need is the maximum, but out of less than half of targeted children
covered under ICDS, only 50 per cent are getting the benefit of supplementary nutrition.

V.        RAJIV GANDHI NATIONAL CRECHE SCHEME FOR THE CHILDREN OF WORKING MOTHERS
 
5.1       The scheme aims to provide day care services for children in the age group of 0-6 years, belonging to economically
weaker sections of society, whose family income does not exceed Rs. 12,000 per month.  The crèches running under the
scheme provide health care, supplementary nutrition, medical check-up and immunization, etc. to the children whose parents
are away at work sites or are incapacitated due to sickness and are unable to look after them. 
 
5.2       The Committee notes that Plan funds being released under the Scheme are being optimally utilized by the
implementing agencies. Allocation   of Rs. 90.00 crores for 2007-08 is at an enhanced level due to increase in the financial
norms from Rs. 18,480/- to Rs. 42,384/- per crèche per annum.  There has been increase in the honorarium for crèche workers
and  component of supplementary nutrition also.  Under the scheme, 90 per cent of the total expenditure is released as grant to
the implementing organization, except the honorarium of crèche workers.
 
5.3       The scheme is implemented through the Central Social Welfare Board and two other national level organizations, i.e.,
Indian Council for Child Welfare and Bhartiya Adim Jati Sevak Sangh. Out of total 30,902 creches running in the country,
24,101 creches are being maintained by the Central Social Welfare Board, 3279 creches by ICCW and 5137 by BAJSS.
 
5.4       The Committee was informed that all these three organizations have experience of implementing crèche programme
across the country for almost three decades and have a nation-wide presence and network for running crèches.   These
organizations are well equipped with field units and staff.  Hence no constraints are being faced for implementation of the
scheme through these organizations. The Committee recommends that to meet the growth in number of creches other
organization/NGOs may also be involved in the implementation of these projects. 
 
5.5       While not disputing the considerable experience of the three implementing agencies handling the Crèche Scheme, the
Committee would like to draw attention to two problem areas.  First is the uneven spread of Creches across the country. Out of
total 30,902 creches in the country, maximum concentration is in Andhra Pradesh (3902), M.P.(2740), Maharashtra (2292),
Tamil Nadu (1928), U.P.(1868) and West Bengal (2203). The Committee strongly feels that there is a need for conducting a
survey across the country so as to bring the uncovered cities under the scheme.   This task can be easily handled by the State
monitoring agencies like State Women Development Corporations, NIPCCD etc.
 
5.6       The other area of concern identified by the Committee is the pendency of settlement of accounts. The Committee notes
that Andhra Pradesh State Board having the maximum number of crèches (3902) has settled accounts upto 1995-96 only. For
States like Assam, Manipur, Rajasthan, Arunachal Pradesh, Mizoram and A&N Islands, accounts have been settled upto 2003-
04 only.  Very few States have settled accounts upto 2005-06.  Evidently, funds are released without settlement of previous
accounts thereby violating the financial rules.  Details about crèches being run by the two other implementing agencies are not
known to the Committee.   The Committee apprehends a similar status with regard to 8659 creches   being run by them.  The
Committee would like to point out that with the enhanced financial norms and levying of user charges, financial management
should be as per the prescribed norms. The Committee wonders about the factors behind non-settlement of accounts by an
experienced body like CSWB having a country-wide network of State Boards for running the crèches.
 
5.7       The Committee notes that the monitoring of crèches which is a continuing process has been assigned to States/Women
study centres of the Universities and State Women Development Corporations during the current financial year.  So far,
feedback has been received from monitoring             agencies in respect of 276 creches being run in the States of Delhi,
Haryana, Jammu & Kashmir, Madhya Pradesh, Manipur, Nagaland, Orissa, Tripura and Uttar Pradesh. The Committee may
be apprised about the feed back on the implementation of the scheme.
 
5.8       The Committee notes that there are a large number of working mothers in unorganized sector who are in great need of
creches to look after their children when they go to work.  The safety of the children is utterly neglected and they are prone to

X.            CENTRAL ADOPTION RESOURCE AGENCY (CARA)
 
10.1     Central Adoption Resource Agency (CARA) was set up in 1990 and has been registered as an autonomous body under
the Registration of Societies Act, 1860. 
 
10.2     It is assigned the role of regulating inter-country adoptions from India and promoting domestic adoption.   For this
purpose, CARA at present has recognized 65  Indian Placement Agencies(RIPAs) to carry out in-country and inter-country
adoptions of children, who are either relinquished by biological parents/unwed mother/guardians or are abandoned/destitute
children and have been declared legally free for adoption by Juvenile Welfare Board/Child Welfare Committee.  There are 128
Enlisted Foreign Adoption Agencies (EFAAs) in over 24 countries including 46 Government Departments enlisted by CARA
for processing the application of foreign/NRI parents for adoption.  There are also 18 Adoption Coordinating agencies (ACAs)
recognized for promoting Indian adoption and to formulate, develop and execute programmes and activities for generating
awareness in this regard.  These agencies also coordinate the activities of its member placement agencies and assist them in
finding Indian parents for their children.  There are no regional offices of CARA at present.  CARA regulates inter-country
adoption through “Guidelines for Adoption from India-2006”.  CARA issued 867 NOCs in the year 2005 and 853 NOCs in the
year 2006 for inter-country adoption.
 
10.3     The Committee notes that in the year 2005, 3151 children were adopted. However, keeping in view large number of

18.3            Committee’s attention has been drawn by a Study entitled ‘Poverty, Gender and Micro-Credit: A study of the
Experience of RMK’ sponsored by the Ministry and carried out by the Centre for Women’s Development Studies, New Delhi
in 2002. This study looks at the RMK experience of six years from March, 1993 to March, 1999.
            The following observations made in the above study are worth noting –
“RMK seeks to extend micro credit, with this over all objective, to women in poverty households.  However,
despite this mandate to focus on poor as defined/ accepted in public policy on cut off household income level,
only a small minority of the assisted borrowers is in BPL income level and only a small percentage (3.9%) is
of ST. Those with <Rs.11000 annual household income are in a minority (20%). The majority are middle and
upper poor.  This exclusion of the poorest, the hard-core poor, results in most of the intended target group
remaining outside the micro credit net.”
          
“The implementation of RMK credit delivery is so NGO specific in respect of the identification and location
details of the borrowers that unless the NGO and its staff are available and they cooperate and provide the
details of the borrowers including their location, it is almost impossible to contact the borrowers and
interview them. There is no visibility of RMK programme as such and the borrowers are quite often not
aware that the funds they have received are RMK funds.”
 
18.4     The Committee may be apprised of the follow-up action initiated on the recommendations of the above study. The
Committee also notes that another study is to be conducted to assess the impact of credit scheme on women beneficiaries
during the last five years. The Committee hopes that this study would be completed at the earliest so that benefits under RMK
reach maximum beneficiaries.
18.5     The Committee in its earlier Report had pointed out that RMK charges interest @ 8% on reducing balance from the
borrowing agency which in turn charges any rate on or above 8% on reducing balance from the ultimate beneficiaries subject
to maximum upto 18%.  Reports have been received by the Committee that there are instances of implementing agencies
charging 24% as interest rate from the beneficiaries. The Committee recommends that this issue need to be looked into and
check should be prevented from doing so and a cap should be put on the interest charged, under this scheme.
 
18.6     The Committee was informed that on the directions of the Governing Board of RMK, a 10 member Sub-Committee
was formed on 21.03.06 which besides other issues, also examined the issue of lowering of interest-rate of RMK.
Recommendation of the Sub-Committee was that the maximum upper limit currently at 18% on reducing balance to 15% on
reducing balance be brought down for RMK loans.  However, the Committee notes that this recommendation of the Sub-
Committee  was not agreed to by the Governing Board. Board was of the view that the position may be reviewed after two
years when RMK may have expanded business.
 
18.7     The Committee is not inclined to agree with the view taken by the Governing Board of RMK.  The Committee
reiterates its earlier recommendation.  The Committee would like to be  apprised about different rates of interest charged on an
average under various loan schemes being implemented under RMK.
 
18.8     The Committee notes the recommendation of the sub-committee in respect of North-eastern region which inter-alia
states that RMK should take immediate steps to promote some of potential NGOs of regions who will co-ordinate and
facilitate the credit linkage to grass root units (SHG/Federations/Co-operatives) with RMK.  As there are very few old
voluntary organizations working in these regions, RMK should promote new organisations by relaxing its lending operational
norms, interest rate, margin etc for quick implementation of its programme. The Committee desires that keeping in view of
special focus on NE region, RMK should immediately take steps to give impetus to NE region.  Besides this, capacity
building, training, skill development, skill upgradation etc are some of the key components of micro-credit programme which
need to be provided to SHG beneficiaries.
 
18.9     The Committee was informed that the functioning of RMK is concentrated in certain States of the country; almost 60
per cent of the loans are going to Tamil Nadu and Andhra Pradesh.  The Committee also notes that the RMK is NGOs driven
scheme. The composition of the RMK itself is such that those who have knowledge of it continue to have knowledge of it,
monopolise the knowledge and in turn monopolise the funds which is not a sustainable concept.   The Committee notes that

shape to the guidelines laid down by the Supreme Court in the Vishaka case.  The Bill is being examined at various

committees set up in the country in terms of the said judgement are not centrally maintained by the Ministry as it has not been
found feasible to do so. However, in the Action Taken Note the Committee was informed that the NCW has issued reminders
to all the organisations and Universities which have not set up complaint committees or which have not furnished any
information in this regard. The Committee would like to be apprised about the information received from various States.  The
Committee recommends that the directions contained in the Supreme Court Judgement in Vishaka case may be implemented
in all the Central Government Departments, and its autonomous and subordinate offices and organizations immediately.   The

XXI.            GENDER BUDGETING
 
21.1     Gender Budgeting is understood as a dissection of the Government budget to establish its gender-differential impacts
and to translate gender commitments into budgetary commitments.Gender Budgeting lends itself to strengthening
administrative processes and actions to achieve the targets for improvement in the position of women.  It not only entails a
look at allocation of resources for women but goes beyond to cover tracking the utilization of allocated resources, impact
analysis and beneficiary incidence analysis of public expenditure and policy from a gender perspective.
 
21.2     The Committee was informed that the Sub-Group on Gender Budgeting was set-up as part of the Working Group on
Empowerment of Women for 11
th Five Year Plan.
Main recommendations of the Working group are:
-         Important National  macro-economic policies to be engendered
-                Review of and effective implementation of all legislations and
-                laws with a gender perspective to eliminate all forms of discrimination
-                and violence against women.
-                Gender mainstreaming to be extended to corporate sector and other
-                civil society organizations
-                Estimation of value addition by women in the unorganized, informal
-                and rural non farm sector and systemized mechanism in place to
               monetize the labour, efforts and output and include the same in the GDP
-                Gender Outcome Assessment
-                Strengthening of Gender Budget cells in all Ministries/ Departments.
 
21.3     So far  50 Ministries/Departments have set up Gender Budgeting (GB) Cells. Detailed training manuals were needed to
be prepared which can be used by the Trainers. These manuals will give the approach and the methodology to be taken in the
engendering policies, schemes, programmes and assessing their gender outcomes. The Committee was informed that a Task
Force for developing a Gender Budgeting Manual is being constituted by the Ministry.
 
21.4     To ensure Gender Budgeting in true sense, in 2006-07 the Ministry adopted a multi pronged strategy to effectively
wield gender budgeting as a tool for women’s empowerment. Initiatives ranged from advocacy, training and capacity building
to strengthening partnerships, supporting policy dialogues and strategy sessions. However, the Committee notes that more pro-
active action is required to be taken to effectively handle the concept of Gender Budgeting. Preparation of training manual
which is indispensable tool of the concept is under formulation by sub-committee. It seems it will take another 2-3 years to
finalise the things. The Committee recommends that immediate step should be taken to finalise the training manual in a time-
bound manner. The Ministry should evolve a monitoring mechanism to ensure that all the Government
Ministries/Departments/Undertakings are taking necessary action for resorting to Gender Budgeting.
 
21.5     It has come to the notice of the Committee that many expenditures being incurred by different Ministries/Departments,
which are not directly women specific were being shown in the Gender budgeting.  This, Committee notes, results in inflated
figures that does not reflect the actual allocation for women.  The Committee recommends that this practice should be stopped
immediately and the Gender budgeting should reflect only those expenditure/allocation that are cent percent women specific.

Metropolitan Magistrate so that the cases are cleared early.   The Committee may be apprised about the number of cases
pending in Juvenile Justice Board alongwith their period of pendency.                               (Para 9.4)
Comments of the Committee
            The Committee is concerned with the reply of the Ministry. It seems no state is ready to hear the plights of children
and the child related issues are not getting required attention of the State Governments. The Committee therefore recommends
that time bound action plan should be made and states should be directed to adhere to the plan. (Para 9.5)
Comments of the Committee
            The Committee recommends that the Ministry should ensure that Juvenile Justice Boards and Welfare Committees are
set up in all States. The Committee notes that the number of Homes assisted under the Programme for Juvenile Justice indicate
that States like Arunachal Pradesh, Himachal Pradesh, Jammu and Kashmir, Jharkhand, Manipur, Uttaranchal and UTs like
Pondicherry, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra and Nagara Haveli, Daman and Diu and Lakshwadweep do
not have even a single such home. Besides that, details furnished indicate that maximum number of such homes are in the
State of Maharashtra.             The Committee would like the Ministry to go deep into the reasons for lack of interest shown by
some of the States and concentration of a very large number of homes in a few States.                                                             
            (Para 9.7)
X.            CENTRAL ADOPTION RESOURCE AGENCY (CARA)
Comments of the Committee
 
            The Committee notes that in the year 2005, 3151 children were adopted. However, keeping in view large number of
children waiting for adoption, the Committee feels that the scheme should be revisited for simplifying procedures.  There is
also need for obtaining feedback from the parents to know their difficulties during adoption after adoption.    The Committee
may also be apprised about the procedure adopted by CARA to monitor the life of the adopted children for a few years after
adoption.            (Para 10.3)
XI.
              NEW SCHEMES
 
Comments of the Committee
 
            Committee’s experience about new schemes proposed to be launched by the Ministry has not been very encouraging.
Committee has been observing that new schemes are proposed without any pre-liminary exercise about formulation of their
components.  A token provision is duly made which continues for years together due to a number of procedural formalities to
be completed at different levels. New schemes should be announced only after the text of the scheme is ready. 
Comprehensive Scheme for Combating Trafficking of Women and Children and Scheme for Relief and Rehabilitation of Rape
Victims are two such schemes. Comprehensive Scheme for Combating Trafficking of Women and Children was introduced
during the Tenth Plan.  As per the information available with the Committee, there was an allocation of Rs. 3.00 crore for the
Scheme in 2004-05, reduced to Rs. 30 lakhs in 2005-06 and Rs. 50 lakhs provided in 2006-07. Provision for 2007-08 is Rs.
1.00 crore. The only progress which seems to have been made is the change in its name. The very fact that it is proposed to be
launched as a new scheme inspite of being in the formulation stage during the Tenth Plan indicates that there is not going to be
any progress in the near future.  Scheme for Relief and Rehabilitation   of Rape Victims is the other scheme which was
introduced in 2006-07 with a token provision of Rs. 1.00 crore. Same provision is there for 2007-08 and it continues to be at
the proposal stage.                                                                                                                           (Para 11.2)
Comments of the Committee
            Rajiv Gandhi Scheme for Empowerment of Adolescent Girls is another new scheme proposed to be launched after
merger of two schemes, Kishori Shakti Yojana and Nutrition Programme for Adolescent Girls. The Committee observes that
NPAG was implemented on a pilot basis in 2002-03 and 2003-04 by the Planning Commission It continued on a pilot project
basis in 51 identified backward districts in 2006-07 also. Kishori Shakti Yojana has been there under ICDS for a few years. It
was only in 2006-07 that the scheme has been expanded from 2000 ICDS projects to 6118 ICDS projects. Committee is not
aware whether there is going to be a significant modification by bringing these two schemes under a new scheme.   The
Committee would, however, like to emphasise that there is a need for having a comprehensive review of all the Schemes
relating to nutrition for women and children being run not only by the Ministry of Women and Child Development but by
other Ministries like Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Rural Development etc.   The Committee strongly feels that there
should be an umbrella scheme for provision of nutrition to women and children under which different small schemes run by
other Ministries can be brought together.                                                                                               (Para 11.3)
Comments of the Committee

and the initiatives taken by them to have a coordinated approach to tackle the problem of malnutrition.                    (Para 11.4)
Comments of the Committee
            The Committee would also like to draw the attention towards the status of National Nutrition Mission which was set up
in 2003. Since then, token provision is being made.   2007-08 also seems to be no exception as a token provision of Rs. 10
lakhs has been made for the proposed launch of National Nutrition Mission.  The Committee views with serious concern
element of undue delay on such a vital issue.  The Committee, accordingly,  recommends that a final decision in this matter
may be taken at the earliest.                                                                                     (Para 11.5)
 
Comments of the Committee
 
            The Committee notes that the Ministry proposes to combine the existing child protection schemes under one Centrally
Sponsored Scheme, Integrated Child Protection Scheme.  Integrated Child Protection Scheme needs to be launched to avoid
any hindrance/ adverse impact on the existing components of different schemes.  The Committee hopes that due care must
have been taken about the drawbacks/ difficulties in the existing schemes and formulation of the new scheme accordingly.
While welcoming the initiative, the Committee would like to point out that all formalities like in principle approval of
Planning  Commission followed by approval from EFC should be completed within the minimum possible time span.  The
Committee notes that separate provision  for all the child protection schemes to be brought under proposed ICDS Scheme and
also for ICPS scheme has been made for 2007-08. This is a clear indication that the proposed ICPS scheme    is likely to
remain in the formulation stage during 2007-08.  The Committee urges upon the Ministry to finalise the Scheme at the
earliest.                                     (Para 11.6)

            OTHER SCHEMES (CHILD WELFARE)
Comments of the Committee
 
            The Committee would like to have full details about proposed interventions under this scheme during 2007-08 for
which enhanced allocation has been made to CSWB for 2007-08.  The Committee would also like to understand the work
done by CSWB under the Innovative Scheme during the Tenth Plan.  The Committee also strongly feels that with a number of
Child Protection Schemes transferred from the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment to the Ministry and the proposed
launching of a new composite scheme by the Ministry, viability of Innovative Scheme as a separate scheme also needs to be
looked into.  The Committee accordingly, recommends that necessary measures may be initiated by the Ministry.      
                                                                                                                                                 (Para 12.3)
Comments of the Committee
 
            The Committee hopes that with the proposed provision of Rs. 10.00 crores for the National Commission for Protection
of Child Rights in 2007-08, the Commission would finally start working. The Committee has also been observing that only a
token provision was being made for ‘Information Technology’ during the Tenth Plan. Position remains unchanged during
2007-08 also. The Committee would like to understand the reasons therefore.                                                                             
                                                                                                                                        (Para 12.4)

         CONDENSED COURSES FOR WOMEN EDUCATION
Comments of the Committee
            The Committee desires that more publicity may be given to the residential courses so that more NGOs are coming
forward to run the scheme.           (Para 13.4)
 
            The Committee is, however, surprised to note that the Report of the Working Group continues to be under the
consideration of the Ministry.  The Committee is of the opinion that with the Eleventh Plan Period starting from 2007-08,
there should not be any further delay and the programme should be implemented in the revised form as recommended by the
Working Group from the first year of the Eleventh Plan Period itself.

Comments of the Committee
 
            The Committee has been expressing its serious concern on the undue delay in arriving at a final decision about the
status of Balika Samridhi Yojana. That scheme has failed to achieve the desired objective   is evident from the availability of
unspent balances  with all the State Govts.  The Committee has also been cautioning the Ministry every year in this regard.

expenditure of Rs. 10.89 crore as on 16.03.07 against an allocation of Rs. 16.00 crore reported in 2006-07. During the entire

Comments of the Committee
 
            The Committee further notes that the judgment of the Supreme Court in the Vishaka case is applicable to all
workplaces/employer’s organizations throughout the country, whether in the public or private sector. Details of the complaints
committees set up in the country in terms of the said judgement are not centrally maintained by the Ministry as it has not been
found feasible to do so. However, in the Action Taken Note the Committee was informed that the NCW has issued reminders
to all the organisations and Universities which have not set up complaint committees or which have not furnished any
information in this regard. The Committee would like to be apprised about the information received from various States.  The
Committee recommends that the directions contained in the Supreme Court Judgement in Vishaka case may be implemented
in all the Central Government Departments, and its autonomous and subordinate offices and organizations immediately.   The
Committee may be apprised about the organizations/Departments of the Central Government which have not taken steps to
implement the direction of the Supreme Court.                                                                          (Para 20.2)

Gender Budgeting. Preparation of training manual which is indispensable tool of the concept is under formulation by sub-
committee. It seems it will take another 2-3 years to finalise the things. The Committee recommends that immediate step
should be taken to finalise the training manual in a time-bound manner. The Ministry should evolve a monitoring mechanism
to ensure that all the Government Ministries/Departments/Undertakings are taking necessary action for resorting to Gender
Budgeting.                                                        (Para 21.4)

            The Committee recommends that this practice should be stopped immediately and the Gender budgeting should reflect

I           INTRODUCTION
 
1.1       The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports, Government of India owes its origin to the Department of Sports, which
was set up in 1982 at the time of the 9
th Asian Games in New Delhi.  During the International Youth Year 1985 it was
upgraded to the Department of Youth Affairs & Sports.  On 17th May, 2000 it became a full fledged Ministry.
 
1.2       The Ministry of Youth Affairs & Sports (MoYAS) is entrusted with the responsibilities relating to the development
of Youth and Adolescents, and the functions of the Central Government with regard to Sports and Physical Education.
 
1.3       The MoYA&S is implementing a large number of schemes for youth and adolescents development.   These
schemes are proposed to be re-oriented as a part of an integrated framework comprising three key thrust areas viz.,
Personality Development, Preparation for Work Participation/Employability, and Empowerment.

1.4       In so far as the subject of Sports is concerned, this figures in the State List of the Constitution.   In view of this, it is
the State Governments who are primarily responsible for the development and promotion of sports.  The MoYA&S in its
effort to complement the State's efforts aims at development of a broad based sports culture throughout the country, and
significantly expanding the pool of talented sportspersons who can be groomed to bring laurels to the country in
international events.  With this in view, a major initiative proposed to be launched by the Ministry is a scheme with the
title 'Panchayat Yuva Khel Abhiyan', which is aimed at creating basic sports infrastructure, and promoting sports activities
at the village/sub-district level, both as a necessary ingredient of youth development and as a means to substantially widen
the catchment for spotting of talent.   The Committee desires that Pancayat Yuva Khel Abhiyan should be finalized at the
earliest and the details in this regard may be furnished to the Committee.
 
1.5       The Committee was informed that the population of the youth and adolescents is nearly 45% of the total
population, and that of the number of persons below the age of 35 is around 75%.   This creates, the Committee feels, a
unique opportunity to take advantage of this "demographic dividend" and also highlights the urgency of addressing the
needs of the youth and adolescents in a comprehensive manner with the objective of creating responsible citizen as well as
a healthy and productive work force.

III        NATIONAL SERVICE SCHEME
 
3.1       National Service Scheme launched in 1969 has primary focus on the development of personality of students
through community service.   Since its inception, more than 2.8 crore students from Universities, Colleges and other
educational Institutions have participated in NSS activities as student volunteers.
 
3.2       The Scheme is implemented through the State Governments. The basic unit of NSS consists of 50 or 100
volunteers and is headed by a Programme Officer at faculty/institution level.  At the University level, the Programme
Officers of affiliated colleges of the concerned University work under the guidance of Programme Coordinators.  At the
State level, all the Universities in the State work under the guidance of a State Liaison Officer.  The State Liaison Cell at
the State headquarters is responsible for ensuring timely release of grants under its jurisdiction and timely submission of
accounts thereof.  The State level Liaison Cell is fully funded by the Central Government.  There are 15 NSS Regional
Centres in the country.  These Regional Centres maintain liaison with the State Governments, Universities, +2 Councils,
Training and Orientation Centres and Training Orientation and Research Centre, Coordinators and Programme Officers.
 
3.3       The Committee notes that every student cannot join NSS as there is a ceiling on the number of volunteers a State
can have. The cap on the number of NSS volunteers, the Committee feels, appears to be incongruous to the objectives of
NSS.   Our efforts should be to provide every student who is desirous of joining NSS, opportunity to do so.  The
Committee feels that finance should not be a problem in achieving this as funds usually remain under utilized.
 
3.4       The Scheme is jointly funded by the Union and State Governments in a ratio of 7:5 in all States, except North East
Region, including Sikkim, and hilly areas, where the ratio is 3:1.  In J&K and all the Union Territories, Kendriya
Vidyalayas and Navodaya Vidyalayas, the programme is entirely funded by Government of India.  The funding to the
State Government for regular activities is Rs. 160/- per volunteer per annum for normal areas and Rs. 200/- per volunteer
per annum for North Eastern States including Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh and other hilly states as notified by the Planning

IV        NEHRU YUVA KENDRA SANGATHAN
 
4.1       Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan (NYKS) is an autonomous body of the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports and
has its presence in 500 districts of the country.  It is one of the largest grassroot level organizations in the world, catering
to more than eight million non-student rural youth enrolled through about 2.53 lakh village based Youth Clubs.  These
Youth Clubs work in areas like education and training, awareness generation, skill development and self-employment,
entrepreneurial development, thrift and co-operation, besides personality development through sports and adventure and
sustained exposure to new ideas and development strategies.   For implementation of the programmes, every district has a
trained cadre of District Youth Coordinator, National Service Volunteers and Youth leaders.  The strength of NYKS is its
vast network of Youth Clubs at the grassroots level.
 
4.2       NYKS accomplishes its task through three categories of programmes:
(1)
               Regular programmes such as Youth Leaders and Youth Club Development, Panchayat Yuva Shakti Abhiyan,
Employment and Income Generation Programme through Rural Business Hub, Cultural Programmes, Mahila
Sashaktikaran Abhiyan, Work Camp, Local Need Based Project, Adventure Promotion Programmes, etc.
(2)               Special Schemes of Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports like National Service Volunteers, Youth
Development Centres, Awards to Outstanding Youth Clubs, Financial Assistance to Youth Clubs, Rural Sports
Clubs, Rural Information Technology Youth Development Centre (RITYDC), Scheme for Development and
Empowerment of Adolescents, Rashtriya Sadbhawana Yojana.
(3)
               Special Programmes undertaken in collaboration with other Ministries and Organizations.  Here in specific
schemes pertaining to Health, Education, Environment, Poverty alleviation, etc. are  undertaken by NYKS,
from time to time, as one of the implementing agencies on behalf of the concerned Ministries/Departments,
including Ministry of YAS.  In this role, the NYKS is practically seen as any other NGO.
 
4.3       Besides, the programmes covered under the above broad categories, NYKS also plans to observe/celebrate
Important National & International Days & Weeks.

4.8       The Committee also notes that there is uneven spread of Youth Clubs/Mahila Mandals across the country.  The
Committee finds that  A & N Islands, Arunachal Pradesh, Chandigarh, Dadar and Nagar Haveli, Daman and Diu, Delhi,
Goa, Lakshdweep, Mizoram, Nagaland, Pondicherry, Sikkim and Tripura do not have adequate number of Youth

4.9       Due to Ministry’s decision not to open new Youth Clubs/Mahila Mandals, the Committee notes, position in these
States/UTs listed above would remain the same.  Now, in view of putting the opening of new Clubs/Mandals on hold in
2007-08, the position is not going to improve.   The Committee feels that instead of taking a decision not to open new
Clubs/Mandals at the national level, at least these deficient States should have been taken up during 2007-08.  The
Committee, therefore, recommends that the expansion of these Clubs/Mandals be taken in these States for 2007-08 itself
and additional funds for this purpose be provided.
 
4.10     On the issue of establishing NYKs in all districts of the country, the Ministry informed that presently 500 districts
were covered, out of the total districts in the country.  The Committee was informed that more NYKs could not be
established since many of the new districts have actually been established by dividing the earlier districts.  In view of this
and also due to restrictions on creation of new posts, it is proposed to extend coverage of Nehru Yuva Kendras to all the
districts in a phased approach, linked to the number and level of activity of Youth Clubs instead of geographic boundary of
revenue districts. Thus, some of the districts which have fewer youth clubs may be required to be brought under one Nehru
Yuva Kendra through a rationalized approach. 
 
4.11     The Committee has some reservations against this approach of the Ministry.  It is of the opinion that delay in
opening the NYK in all the districts would affect the effective control and monitoring of the Youth Clubs/Mahila
Mandals.  It might lead to some kind of jurisdictional as well as functional problems.  Thus, absence of NYK in district,
would have adverse impact on the functioning of the Clubs/Mandals.  The Committee in the light of its reservations,
desires that all out efforts be made to provide the NYK in remaining districts of the country in a phased manner without

of the NYKS budget was being appropriated for their development.    The Committee is of the opinion that the Ministry

4.14     The Committee notes that except for Vocational Training Programme, Local Need Based Programme & Cultural
Programme, the participation of women in 12 odd programmes run by the NYKS, is poor.  It is needless to say that women
have played more effective role in the kind of programmes NYK implements.   The existing 37 per cent women-
participation, by all means, does not represent the desirable level.   The Committee reiterates that it should be raised upto
60% as recommended in the 190th Report of the Committee.
 
4.15     The Committee is not aware of the number of women among the NYKS functionaries.  It desires that the Ministry
furnish details in this regard to the Committee.
 
4.16     The Ministry has proposed to reorient the existing Schemes of Youth Development Centres (YDCs) and Rural
Information Technology Youth Development Centres (RITYDCs) in the 11
th Plan, which were so far being implemented
as components of the Scheme pertaining to Financial Assistance to Rural Youth and Sports Clubs. It is proposed that a
Youth Development Centres would be established in a modified conceptual framework, as a District Youth Development
Centre (DYDC) at each District Headquarters and a Block Youth Development Centres (BYDC) at each Block
headquarters.  The management of these centres would be carried out through designated management committees on a
self sustained basis.
 
4.17     The Committee has no idea of the changes that will be introduced in RITYDCs during the XI Plan.  Till date, one
Youth Development Centre in each district was intended to be upgraded as RITYDC and a grant of Rs. 1.20 lakh was
provided for it.  The Tenth Plan had a target of establishing 500 RITYDs but the Ministry could establish only 235
RITYDCs.  A number of questions, such as, whether the RITYDCs will also be established on the pattern of YDCs at both
district as well as block level, how can these RITYDCs become an effective instrument in bridging digital gap, the
beneficiaries intended and their level of skill acquirement, etc. needs to be taken into account.   The Committee fears that
unless these things were thoroughly examined, the proposed reorientation in the XIth Plan may not have the desired
results.  
 
4.18     The recruitment process to the post of District Youth Coordinators was cancelled by the competent authority on the
grounds inter-alia that the posts had not been sanctioned by the Ministry of Finance, a number of complaints had been
received about the recruitment process.  Some of the applicants had also moved to the Court against the non-declaration of
the result due to cancellation of the recruitment process. The Hon’ble High Court of Delhi in its Order dated 03.03.1999
directed the respondents to declare the results of the examination and stated that, if the petitioners are found successful, they
should be appointed. On appeal, this order was set aside by the two-judge bench of the same court on 02.08.2000 and the
case was remanded back to the single judge bench for fresh consideration and decision. The matter is sub-judice.
 
4.19     The Committee would like the Ministry to make all efforts for an early settlement of the case.  The Committee would
like to state that whenever the recruitment process is restarted, the candidates of the impugned recruitment process should be
given preference.
 
4.20     Another related aspect is of the creation of new posts necessitated due to proposed expansion of NYKS in the
remaining districts of the country.  Besides, there are large number of vacancies that are waiting to be filled up.  In view of
this, the Committee finds that NYKS is currently highly short of manpower affecting thereby the implementation and
effectivity of its schemes adversely.   The Committee, therefore, recommends that these aspects need to be taken up on

priority, particularly with the Ministry of Finance and Planning Commission, to expedite the creation of new as well as
recruitment of existing posts at various levels in NYKS. 
 
4.21     The Committee has learnt that the NYKS is being involved in the schemes/programmes not only of its parent
Ministry but also of other Ministries/Departments.  The Committee is of the opinion that the District Nehru Yuva Kendras

extra responsibilities only when there is a scope for it in terms of time, resource, expertise etc.
 
V         RASHTRIYA SADBHAVANA YOJANA
 
5.1       The Rashtriya Sadhbhavana Yojana was launched in 2005 in place of the erstwhile National Reconstruction Corps
Scheme.  The Scheme aims at encouraging leadership among the rural youth.  Under the scheme average of around 10-20
volunteers in each of the 500 districts having presence of NYKS are to be enrolled as Nehru Yuva Sathees (NYSs).   These
NYSs are to be nominated by the selected best Youth Clubs and Youth Development Centres in the block and district
respectively.  During 2006-07, 4925 NYSs were deployed through NYKS.
 
5.2       The Committee notes that the performance of the scheme of Rashtriya Sadbhavna Yojna has been uneven in
different states.  The Ministry has informed that this is mainly on account of a requirement that the Youth Clubs, for this
purpose, should be registered for at least three years. However, this requirement could not be fulfilled since many Youth
Clubs could not get registered in many States like UP, Bihar as there are difficulties in getting registration in these States. 
As a result, the scheme suffered.  The Ministry has also submitted that there were some practical difficulties in the actual
selection of Nehru Yuva Sathees (NYSs).   The Ministry has not furnished any information as to what steps it took to
persuade the States to simplify the registration process.  The Committee only hopes that the Ministry must have taken the
matter of slow registration of clubs with concerned States to resolve it.  The Committee, in view of practical problems
being faced in selection of NYSs, regrets to say that these problems still persist.  The Committee recommends the Ministry
to take urgent steps to remove the difficulties encountered in the actual selection of Nehru Yuva Sathees.
5.3       One of the measures taken by the Ministry to improve the situation is to raise the level of honorarium for Nehru
Yuva Sathees from Rs. 1000/- to Rs.1500/-.  The committee welcomes this raise but is afraid that in the face of rising
inflation and other factors, even this raise may not be sufficient to encourage the volunteers to come forth as Nehru Yuva
Sathis.  The Committee is of the opinion that Rs. 1500 may not be at all adequate for areas like J&K, North-East,
Himachal Pradesh and Uttrakhand.
 
5.4       The Committee also welcomes the fact that Rashtriya Sadhbhavana Yojana has been included as a monitorable
programme in the revised 20 Point Programme.   It hopes that this inclusion will ensure proper implementation of the
Scheme.
 
5.5       The Committee notes that BE 2007-08 for the Yojana is pegged at Rs. 8.00 crore which is an enhancement to Rs.
5.00 crore that the Yojana got in RE 2006-07.  The Committee is, however, surprised to see that not a single rupee has
been spent till 31.12.2006 against an allocation of Rs. 5.00 crore.  The Committee would like to know the reasons behind
this complete non-utilization of funds.  It further desires to know as to how the Ministry could reach an achievement of
4925 volunteers against a target of 5911 fixed for the year 2006-07, without spending a single rupee until 31.12.2006.  The
Committee requests the Ministry to throw more light on this.
 
VI        PROMOTION OF NATIONAL INTEGRATION PROGRAMME
 
6.1       The Scheme of Promotion of National Integration was launched as a Central Scheme to provide the youth from
different parts of the country, and from diverse cultural backgrounds, opportunities to interact with each other, know each
others' customs and lifestyles, to work together in community service projects and, in the process, make them aware of the
underlying unity amidst diversity in the country and promote the sprit of national and emotional integration among the
youth.             
 
6.2       The Committee notes that Plan allocation saw a reduction to Rs. 6.15 crore (including NE) in RE 2006-07 from BE
of Rs. 10.00 crore.  However BE 2007-08 provides for enhanced allocation of Rs. 11.50 crore (including NE Region).  As
per the Ministry, the higher allocation under National Integration Programme is due to its importance for youth in the
present context.  The Ministry has been organizing Home Stay Exchange programme for youth of north-eastern states and
J&K to other parts of the country.  This will be strengthened and made two way process in which the youth from other

parts of the country will also be participating in J&K and NE States under the aegis of NYKS.   National and State level
programmes will be conducted for involving youth in the commemoration of the 150 th Year of First War of India's
Independence, 1857.  In addition, assistance will also be provided to State Governments/UTs for organizing State Level
National Integration Camps/Inter State Youth Exchange Programmes and to Non-Government organizations for specific
proposals.
 
6.3       The Committee notes that during 2005-06, against a financial target of Rs. 4.95 crore, the Ministry actually spent
Rs. 5.22 crore.  However, despite the higher expenditure, the physical targets could not be achieved.   For example, as
against a target of 250 programmes in 2005-06, only 18 programmes could be organized.   The Committee notes from the
Outcome Budget, 2007-08, that the reason for this low achievement is perhaps due to non-viable proposals coming from
NGOs/Associations/Institutions.  If this is the case, the Committee wonders as to how so much fund was spent under the
programme.  The Committee would like the Ministry to throw light on this aspect.
 
6.4       It is given to understand that the procedure is being streamlined and the guidelines revised.  The Committee would
like to know about these guidelines and their implementation.

In meanwhile 16 UCs pending to 2003-04 and 2004-05 have been issued.  The Committee is not happy with the level of

to get the pending UCs liquidated on urgent basis and at the same time also ensure that there is no recurrence of such
tendency in future.
 
VII
       NATIONAL SERVICE VOLUNTEERS SCHEME
 
7.1       The National Service Volunteer Scheme provides a platform for the youth to take up a leadership role in the

195th Report of Connittee On Human Resource Development

spheres of the social and community service at the grass roots level.
 
7.2       The Service Volunteer is a youth social worker who is willing to commit his/her energy and time to the service of
the community and the country. The National Service Volunteer Scheme provides for an opportunity for first work
experience after education and is aimed to inculcate leadership qualities in them.  During their deployment, the Volunteers
are paid Rs. 1000/- per month by way of honorarium.  The NSVs, together with the Nehru Yura Sathees (NYSs) under
Rsahtriya Sadhbhavana Yojana, are the backbone of the NYKS.
 
7.3       The Committee notes that the Plan allocation in BE 2007-08 for National Service Volunteers Scheme has been
increased to Rs. 13.50 crores as compared to Rs. 6.00 crores in 2006-07.  The Ministry has informed that the reasons for
seeking increase in allocation for 2007-08 is the proposal to enhance the stipends of the volunteers from the existing Rs.
1000/- per month to Rs. 2500/- per month.  The Committee welcomes the enhancement in the stipends of the volunteers
but it still feels that this enhancement is not sufficient, given the fact that as NSVs, they contribute significantly for social
work on a full time basis. The Committee recommends further enhancement in the stipend of the Volunteers. 
 
7.4       The Scheme aims at deploying 4400 NSVs during 2007-08.  Under the scheme, the volunteers are enrolled in the
beginning of the year and allotted to Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan and National Service Scheme.   The recruitment is
made by a District level Committee headed by the collectors. 
 
7.5       The Committee notes that there is a little awareness about the existence of such a scheme in the public.   The
Committee emphasizes the need for giving a wider publicity about the scheme, mode of recruitment of volunteers, etc.
 
7.6       The Committee further notes that 30 per cent of NSVs after the training remain unemployed and only 30 per cent
become social worker.  The Committee feels that with this achievement, the scheme has failed to create a desirable impact
on our youth particularly to join social sector in a big way.
 
7.7       The Committee notes that these NSVs are associated with NYKs.  However, given the fact that only 500 districts in
the country have NYKs, the youth of remaining districts are being deprived of the opportunity to become NSVs.   Further,
with the projection of only 4400 NSVs to be deployed during 2007-08, the number of volunteers for a district comes to
mere 8 volunteers per district.  The Committee feels that this is an inadequate number.  It only hopes that NSVs are being
selected from uncovered districts as well.
 
7.8       The Committee takes note of the fact that about 5% of NSVs leave midway for various reasons.  The Committee
would like the Ministry to inform it about the impact this drop out has on the scheme and the steps taken to control it.
 
VIII      YOUTH HOSTELS
 
8.1       Youth Hostels are built to promote youth travel within the country.  They have been conceived as a joint venture
between the Central and the State Government.   While the Central Government bears the cost of construction, the State
Government provides fully developed land free of cost with water, electricity, approach road and staff quarters.  After
completion, Youth Hostels are handed over to the State Government  for management.  Youth hostels are generally located
in areas of historical and cultural value, educational centre, tourist importance etc. where facilities for youth activities are
available.  As on 31
st December, 2006, 73 Youth Hotels have been constructed and 20 hostels are under construction and
32 have been approved in principle.   So far, 14 Youth Hostels have been constructed in the North Eastern Region, which
are functional.
 
8.2       The Committee notes that the budgetary allocation for Youth Hostels has decreased to Rs. 1.25 crore in BE 2007-
08 in comparison to Rs. 3.50 crore allocated in RE 2006-07.  This reduction has been made in view of lower actual
expenditure till September, 2006 under Youth Hostel Scheme.   The Committee notes with concern the continuously low
utilization of funds under this scheme.  Against an allocation of Rs. 4.50 crore in 2005-06, the Ministry could utilize only
1.49 crore.  Further in 2006-07, against an allocation of Rs. 3.50 crore, the Ministry could spend a mere 7 lakh only till
31.12.2006.  The extremely low utilization of funds has severely affected the construction of Youth Hostels.  The
Committee is perturbed over such a poor performance of an important scheme from its inception.   It recommends the
Ministry to make effort to improve the situation and devise specific measures to address various problems associated with
this scheme.
